title: NFL: NFC North Preview and Breakdown
excerpt: The NFC North heats up in 2025! Detroit Lions (15-2 last year) are favored at 11-1 Super Bowl odds, led by Jared Goff's precision and a healthier defense. Green Bay Packers chase a title with Jordan Love turning 27—echoing Favre and Rodgers' championship ages—and explosive balance. Minnesota Vikings reload trenches for J.J. McCarthy's debut. Chicago Bears rebuild under Ben Johnson to boost Caleb Williams.Who takes the crown? Dive into the full preview for in-depth analysis.
content:
NFC North Overview

The NFC North stands as one of the NFL's most competitive divisions entering the 2025 season. Last year, it boasted the league's best collective record at 45-23, a .662 winning percentage. Led by the 15-2 Detroit Lions, followed by the 14-3 Minnesota Vikings, 11-6 Green Bay Packers, and 5-12 Chicago Bears, the division sent three teams to the playoffs—though all suffered decisive losses: Detroit fell 55-23 at home, Green Bay 22-10 in Philadelphia, and Minnesota 27-9 to the LA Rams. With four offensive-minded head coaches—Dan Campbell (Lions), Kevin O'Connell (Vikings), Matt LaFleur (Packers), and Ben Johnson (Bears)—and DraftKings Super Bowl odds ranging from Detroit at 11-1 to Chicago at 40-1, the focus is on quarterback transitions, trench battles, and defensive improvements. Only Detroit has never reached a Super Bowl, while the others seek returns absent since 2006 (Bears), 2010 (Packers), and 1976 (Vikings). Statistically, three teams ranked top-10 in scoring offense (Lions 1st at 33 PPG, Packers 8th at 27, Vikings 9th at 25.4) and defense (Vikings 5th at 19.5 allowed, Packers 6th at 19.9, Lions 7th at 20.1), with Chicago lagging at 28th offensively (18.2) and 13th defensively (21.8). Pass rush highlights include Minnesota's 49 sacks (4th) and Green Bay's 45 (8th), while kickers like Detroit's Jake Bates (26/29) and Green Bay's Brandon McManus (20/21) provide reliability.

Chicago Bears

The Bears, mired in mediocrity with no winning season since 2018 and last-place finishes in seven of the past 11 years, underwent a massive overhaul. New head coach Ben Johnson, formerly Detroit's offensive coordinator, brings a balanced, explosive scheme emphasizing under-center snaps (56% in Detroit last year) and play-action passes (36%). He's joined by offensive coordinator Declan Doyle and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, ex-Saints head coach. GM Ryan Poles, extended through 2029, invested heavily in free agency: Pro Bowl guard Joe Thuney (Chiefs), Jonah Jackson (Rams), and center Drew Dalman (Falcons) to bolster the interior line after allowing a league-worst 68 sacks. Defensively, they added Grady Jarrett (Falcons) and Odafe Oweh (Colts). Receivers Ola Zaccheaus (Commanders) and Devin Duvernay (punt/kick returner) replace Keenan Allen (700+ yards lost), while blocking tight end Durham Smythe (Dolphins) joins. Departures include linemen Kevin Zeitler, Larry Borom, Matt Pryor, and Coleman Shelton; ends DeMarcus Walker and Jacob Martin; and DT Byron Cowart.

In the draft, Chicago surprised with TE Colston Loveland (Michigan, 10th overall) to pair with Cole Kmet, WR Luther Burden (Missouri, 2nd round) for yards-after-catch explosiveness, OT Azi Ezirim (Boston College, 2nd) to compete at left tackle, DT Shamar Turner (Texas A&M, 2nd), LB Reuben Hyppolite (Maryland, 4th, 4.37 speed), CB Zah Frazier (UTSA, 5th), and RB Kyle Monangai (Rutgers, 7th, Pacheco-like grinder).

Offense: Johnson aims to transform a unit ranked 32nd in yards, 31st in passing, and 25th in rushing. QB Caleb Williams, after a rocky rookie year (3,500 yards, 20 TDs, 6 INTs but 21% off-target throws and 23% completion on 20+ yard passes), must adapt to under-center footwork (only 84 such throws in college) and release quicker (28 sacks held ball 5+ seconds). Backups Tyson Bagent (solid in spot starts) and veteran Case Keenum provide depth. RB DeAndre Swift (959 yards, 6 TDs, 3.8 YPC) reunites with Johnson, complemented by Roschon Johnson (short-yardage) and Monangai. Receivers DJ Moore (extension; down to 9.9 YPC last year) and Rome Odunze (700+ yards) lead, with Zaccheaus, Burden, and Duvernay adding speed. TEs Kmet (2,600 yards, 17 TDs since 2020) and Loveland enable 12 personnel. The line's interior (Thuney, Dalman, Jackson) strengthens, but tackles Darnell Wright and Braxton Jones (or Ezirim/Kirby Amegadjie) must prove edge protection.

Defense: Allen introduces complex fronts, disguised coverages, and aggressive press man. After starting 4-2 (17.2 PPG allowed) but collapsing to 1-10 (25+ PPG), they ranked 28th against the run (29th YPC). New DTs Jarrett and Turner, plus Oweh (versatile end/tackle, 16.5 career sacks) and Gervon Dexter (5 sacks), join Andrew Billings for interior push. Edge Montez Sweat (5.5 sacks) needs a rebound; Austin Booker or Daniel Hardy complements. LBs Tremaine Edmunds (100+ tackles in 7 seasons) and T.J. Edwards (140+ tackles, 4 sacks) anchor, with Hyppolite vying for the third spot after Jack Sanborn's departure. The secondary shines: CBs Jaylon Johnson (70 starts, 49 PBUs, 7 INTs), Tyrique Stevenson, and nickel Kyler Gordon (207 tackles, 5 INTs); safeties Kevin Byard (130 tackles) and Jaquan Brisker (concussion-limited but versatile). Depth includes Terell Smith, Frazier, Elijah Hicks, and Jonathan Owens. Special teams feature punter Tory Taylor (41.6 net yards) and kicker Cairo Santos (21/25, game-winner vs. Packers).

Outlook: With Williams earning Johnson's trust through audibles and pre-snap motion, Chicago could climb from the basement. Improved trenches and pass-catchers signal progress, but quarterback adaptation and edge depth are key. Expect 7-10 wins if the run defense holds.

Detroit Lions

The Lions, fresh off a 15-2 season and NFC's No. 1 seed, seek redemption after a 45-31 playoff loss to Washington—their first home-field advantage in franchise history. At 27-7 over two years (NFL's best), GM Brad Holmes and coach Dan Campbell emphasize aggression (33 fourth-down attempts, 67% success). Changes include new coordinators: OC John Morton (ex-Jets, Broncos) replaces Ben Johnson; DC Kelvin Sheppard (37, ex-Glenn assistant) replaces Aaron Glenn. Offensive line shifts: Graham Glasgow to center after Frank Ragnow's retirement and Kevin Zeitler's departure; rookies Tate Ratledge (Georgia, 2nd) and Miles Frazier (LSU, 4th) compete inside. Draft picks: DT Tyree Wilson (Ohio State, 1st), WR Isaac Umesi (Arkansas, 3rd), EDGE Ahmed Hassanein (Boise State, 6th), S Dan Jackson (7th), WR Dominic Lovett (Georgia, 7th). Free agents: CB D.J. Reed (Jets), LBs Zack Cunningham and Grant Stuart, S Ifeatu Melifonwu depth, DT Ray-Ray Lopez. Returns from injury: EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, Marcus Davenport, LB Derrick Barnes, Alex Anzalone. Losses: EDGE Za'Darius Smith, LBs Ben Niemann and Jalen Reeves-Maybin, CB Carlton Davis, S C.J. Gardner-Johnson.

Offense: Morton inherits a top unit (2nd yards, 1st scoring at 33 PPG, 6th rush, 2nd pass, 3rd red zone at 70%, 4th third down at 48%). QB Jared Goff (4,629 yards, 37 TDs, 8.6 YPA, 72% completion; elite vs. man at 71%, 20 TDs, 0 INTs) excels pre-snap (RCE: recognize, communicate, execute). Backup Hendon Hooker unproven. RBs Jahmyr Gibbs (1,412 rush, 517 rec yards) and David Montgomery (punishing, 2+ YAC) fuel 146 YPG rushing; play both together for versatility. Receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown (115 catches, 1,263 yards, 12 TDs; blocks like TE) and Jameson Williams (58 catches, improved YAC) lead; Tim Patrick, Umesi, Kalif Raymond (gadgets), and Lovett add depth. TEs Sam LaPorta (60 catches, 726 yards, 7 TDs) and Brock Wright (blocker) versatile. Line: LT Taylor Decker (injury-prone), LG Christian Mahogany, C Glasgow, RG Ratledge, RT Penei Sewell; interior youth a concern.

Defense: Sheppard, influenced by Lou Anarumo and Steve Spagnuolo, reduces blitzes (37% last year) and man coverage with healthier personnel. Ranked 7th scoring (20.1 allowed). EDGE Hutchinson (7.5 sacks in 4.5 games pre-injury) and Davenport return; Van Ness, Enagbare, and Josh Paschall depth. DTs Alim McNeill (knee recovery), D.J. Reader, Wilson, and Lopez anchor run defense. LBs Jack Campbell (131 tackles), Anzalone (63 tackles, 7 TFLs), Barnes (situational rusher); backups Rodriguez (injured), Cunningham, Stuart. Safeties Kerby Joseph (9 INTs, range) and Brian Branch (Pro Bowl versatile); third safety Maddox or Jackson. CBs Terrion Arnold (emerging, 325 man snaps as rookie), Reed ($40M), nickel Amik Robertson; depth Rocky Ya-Sin, Khalil Dorsey. Special teams elite: K Bates (26/29, 19 straight to start), P Jack Fox (46.2 net record), returner Raymond (13.8 YPR); coach Dave Fipp key.

Outlook: A brutal road slate (at GB, BAL, CIN, KC, WAS, PHI, LAR, MIN) tests depth, but returning health and grit position Detroit as favorites. 13-4 possible if interior line holds and pass rush elevates.

Minnesota Vikings

The 14-3 Vikings finished second but faltered late, losing 31-9 to Detroit for the division and 27-9 (9 sacks allowed) to the Rams in playoffs. Coach Kevin O'Connell (34-17, 0-2 playoffs) hands keys to QB J.J. McCarthy after injury-wiped rookie year. Spent $267M on free agents (2nd most), focusing trenches: C Ryan Kelly ($18M/2yrs), RG Will Fries ($88M), DTs Jonathan Allen ($51M/3yrs) and Javon Hargrave ($30M/2yrs). Added QB Sam Howell, RB Jordan Mason (trade from SF), WR Rondale Moore. Draft: OG Donovan Jackson (Ohio State, 1st), WR Tykee Felton (Maryland, 3rd), DT Ty'Ron Hopper (Georgia, 5th), LB Kobe King (Penn State, 5th), TE Gavin Bartholomew (Pitt, 6th). Losses massive: QBs Sam Darnold (4,300 yards, 35 TDs to SEA), Daniel Jones (to IND), Nick Mullens (to JAX); RB Cam Akers; OL Cam Robinson, David Quessenberry, Ed Ingram, Dalton Risner, Garrett Bradbury; EDGE Patrick Jones (7 sacks), DTs Jonathan Bullard, Jerry Tillery; CBs Stephon Gilmore, Shaquil Griffin; S Camryn Bynum (to IND).

Offense: O'Connell's pass-heavy scheme (3rd in pass yards at 257/game, 4th in pass TDs at 95 over 3yrs) seeks balance (27th rush attempts, 29th YPC). McCarthy (27-1 at Michigan) brings athleticism; backups Howell, Brett Rypien, Josh McCown. RBs Aaron Jones (1,000+ rush, 50+ catches) and Mason (789 yards) complement; FB C.J. Ham for more 21 personnel (12% last year). Line: LT Christian Darrisaw (injury return), LG Jackson (rookie), C Kelly, RG Fries, RT Brian O'Neill; injuries to Kelly/Fries a risk. WRs Justin Jefferson (7,432 yards over 5 yrs, 96 YPG) and Jordan Addison (900 yards, 9 TDs; suspended early) star; Jalen Nailor (6 TDs), Felton depth; Moore injured. TE T.J. Hockenson (rebound from 40 catches post-injury) and Josh Oliver. Improve short-yardage (27th 4th-down, 46%).

Defense: Brian Flores' blitz-heavy unit (41%, 49% last year; 1st takeaways at 33) ranked 5th scoring (19.5 allowed), 2nd run. EDGE Jonathan Greenard (12 sacks), Andrew Van Ginkel (11.5, 2 pick-6s), Dallas Turner (290 snaps), Gabriel Murphy. DTs Allen/Hargrave (new, injury returns), NT Harrison Phillips (body-snatcher), Jalen Redmond. LBs Blake Cashman (111 tackles, 4.5 sacks), Ivan Pace Jr. (69 tackles, 3 sacks), Eric Wilson (depth). S Harrison Smith (14th year, 35+ INTs/20+ sacks elite club), Metellus/Ward/Jackson battle opposite. CBs Jeff Okudah (4th team), Isaiah Rodgers ($11M/2yrs), nickel Byron Murphy (6 INTs, $54M); depth Mekhi Blackmon, Aubrey Pleasant, Dwight McGlothern. K Will Reichard (24/30), but returns last (punt 31st kickoff).

Outlook: Roster turnover and McCarthy's inexperience temper expectations, but trenches and Jefferson/Addison could yield 10-7. Early schedule (at CHI, vs. ATL/CIN) key; health of free agents critical.

Green Bay Packers

The 11-6 Packers, third in the North, boast NFC's best record since 2019 (67-33) under Matt LaFleur. Youngest team (25.3 avg age), they ranked top-8 in scoring offense (27 PPG) and defense (19.9 allowed). Plus-12 turnover margin (3rd); plus-46 since 2019 (2nd). Went 0-6 vs. MIN/DET/PHI last year. New QB coach Sean Mannion, OC Nathaniel Hackett returns. Free agents: LG Aaron Banks ($47M from SF), CB Nate Hobbs ($48M from LV), LB Isaiah Simmons, WR Mecole Hardman. Draft: WR Matthew Golden (Texas, 1st, 4.29 speed), OT Anthony Belton (NC State, 2nd), WR Sevyn Banks (TCU, 3rd), EDGE Barron Sorrento (Texas, 4th). Losses: CBs Jaire Alexander (injuries), Eric Stokes; C Josh Myers; DT T.J. Slaton; LB Eric Wilson; RB A.J. Dillon. New president Ed Policy.

Offense: Run-heavy (51% runs, 3rd) with explosiveness (70 10+ yard runs, 59 20+ yard passes, 14 40+). QB Jordan Love (3,389 yards, 25 TDs; 14% throws 20+ yards) turns 27; must cut INTs (22 last 2yrs) and boost accuracy (63%). Backup Malik Willis (74%, 550 yards in relief). RB Josh Jacobs (1,329 yards, 15 TDs) leads; Emanuel Wilson (502 yards), Chris Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd (injury return). WRs Golden (versatile), Dontayvion Wicks (76 targets), Romeo Doubs (72, contract year), Jayden Reed (75, gadgets); Christian Watson (knee, midseason return); drops (29) addressed. TEs Tucker Kraft (50 catches, 707 yards, 7 TDs), Luke Musgrave. Line: LT Rasheed Walker (competes with Morgan/Belton), LG Banks, C Elgton Jenkins (move from guard, back injury), RG Sean Rhyan, RT Zach Tom ($88M).

Defense: Jeff Hafley's simulated pressures and disguises yield 31 turnovers (4th), 17 INTs (3rd), 45 sacks. 7th vs. run (<100 YPG). EDGE Rashan Gary (7.5 sacks), Lukas Van Ness (7 career), Kingsley Enagbare (4.5), Brenton Cox Jr. (4), Sorrento. DTs Kenny Clark (Pro Bowler, foot recovery), Devonte Wyatt (emerging), Carl Brooks. LBs Edgerrin Cooper (77 tackles, 3.5 sacks; +20 lbs muscle), Quay Walker (100+ tackles 3yrs), Isaiah McDuffie (94). Safeties Xavier McKinney (8 INTs), Evan Williams (rookie starter). CBs Hobbs, Keisean Nixon (versatile), nickel Javon Bullard; Bo Melton (WR convert), Micah Abraham depth. Special teams: K McManus (20/21), returner Nixon (2x Pro Bowl).

Outlook: Balanced and young, Green Bay eyes Super Bowl with Love's growth and fast start (vs. DET/WAS). Edge rush must elevate vs. elites for 12-5 and division crown.

Overall Summary
